Which image format do exam forms accept?

Why exam portals ask for JPG, what goes wrong with PNG and HEIC, and how to convert without losing quality.

Almost every form wants JPG

JPG, also written JPEG, is what Indian exam portals overwhelmingly ask for. It is old, universally supported, and crucially it lets the file size be tuned smoothly, which is how a portal can demand a photo between 20 and 50 KB and expect people to comply.

That last point explains the preference. You cannot ask for a PNG of a specific kilobyte size in any meaningful way, because PNG compression is lossless and the size is whatever the image content happens to produce.

Why PNG causes trouble

PNG is excellent for screenshots, logos and anything with sharp edges or transparency. For photographs it produces much larger files, often five to ten times the size of an equivalent JPG, which puts you over the ceiling immediately.

Renaming a PNG to end in .jpg does not convert it. The file begins with bytes that identify the format, and any server checking properly will see a PNG regardless of what the name says. You need a real re-encode, which any resizer performs when it outputs a JPG.

Transparency is a second trap. A PNG with a transparent background converts to JPG with that area filled, and if the converter fills it with black you get a photo with a black background. Good converters fill with white.

HEIC, the iPhone problem

Recent iPhones save photos as HEIC by default. It is a genuinely better format, roughly half the size of JPG at similar quality, and almost no Indian exam portal accepts it. Many will not even recognise the file enough to give you a sensible error.

You can switch the camera itself. Open Settings, then Camera, then Formats, and choose Most Compatible. New photos will be JPG. Existing HEIC photos need converting, which any resizer that reads HEIC will do as part of its normal output.

Sharing a HEIC photo through WhatsApp converts it to JPG as a side effect, which is a common workaround. Be aware it also compresses the image heavily, so you lose quality you may need for a large photograph.

WEBP and the others

WEBP turns up when you save an image from a website. Support in exam portals is close to zero. Convert it to JPG before you try.

PDF is occasionally requested for documents like a handwritten declaration, but almost never for a photograph. Read the notification carefully, since sending a PDF where a JPG was wanted fails silently on some portals.

Converting without losing quality

Every JPG save discards a little detail. Converting once, from your original file, is fine. Converting a file that has already been through WhatsApp, then through a compressor, then through a resizer, stacks the losses and shows.

Start from the original in your camera roll every time, and do the resize and the format conversion in one step rather than several. That single habit produces noticeably better results than any amount of fiddling afterwards.
